commands.name: GetProjectInfo
commands.description: Retrieves information about the currently loaded project.

isUntitled.description: True, if the project is not saved yet.

isTeamwork.description: True, if the project is a Teamwork (BIMcloud) project.

projectLocation.description: The location of the project in the filesystem or a BIMcloud project reference. A BIMcloud project reference is returned without the user name and login token.

projectPath.description: The path of the project. A filesystem path or a BIMcloud server relative path.

example.description: Prints the name, path and Teamwork state of the open project with GetProjectInfo.
example.code:
"""Prints the name, path and Teamwork state of the open project with GetProjectInfo."""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectInfo'))

commands.name: GetProjectInfoFields
commands.description: Retrieves the names and values of all project info fields.

example.description: Prints the id, name and value of every Project Info field with GetProjectInfoFields.
example.code:
"""Prints the id, name and value of every Project Info field with GetProjectInfoFields."""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectInfoFields'))

commands.name: SetProjectInfoField
commands.description: Sets the value of a project info field.

projectInfoId.description: The id of the project info field.

projectInfoValue.description: The new value of the project info field. An empty string clears the field.

example.description: Sets the value of the first Project Info field with SetProjectInfoField, reads it back, then restores it.

commands.name: CreateProjectInfoFields
commands.description: Creates one or more custom project info fields. From Archicad 30 the Project Info group of each field can be given; without it the field goes to the first group.

projectInfoFields.description: Array of custom project info fields to create.

example.description: Creates a custom Project Info field with CreateProjectInfoFields, then deletes it again. From Archicad 30 the new field goes to the first Project Info group unless projectInfoGroupId is given.

commands.name: DeleteProjectInfoFields
commands.description: Deletes one or more custom project info fields, by their autotext keys or, from Archicad 30, by the ids of the fields of the Project Info groups. Hardcoded fields cannot be deleted.

projectInfoIds.description: List of project info field ids (autotext keys, as GetProjectInfoFields returns them) to delete. Only custom fields can be deleted. On Archicad 30 a key is matched to the field by its name, so it fails when more than one field has the name; delete such a field by its projectInfoFieldId instead.

projectInfoFieldIds.description: List of fields of the Project Info groups to delete, by the ids GetProjectInfoGroups returns. Available from Archicad 30. Their results follow the results of projectInfoIds.

example.description: Creates a custom Project Info field and deletes it by its autotext key with DeleteProjectInfoFields. Built-in fields cannot be deleted. From Archicad 30 fields can also be deleted by projectInfoFieldIds.

commands.name: RenameProjectInfoFields
commands.description: Renames custom fields of the Project Info groups. Fixed (built-in) fields cannot be renamed. Available from Archicad 30.

projectInfoFields.description: The fields of the Project Info groups to rename, each with its new name. Fixed (built-in) fields cannot be renamed.

name.description: The new name of the field. It must not be used by another field.

example.description: Creates a custom Project Info field, renames it with RenameProjectInfoFields, then deletes it. Built-in fields cannot be renamed. Requires Archicad 30 or later.

commands.name: MoveProjectInfoFields
commands.description: Moves fields of the Project Info groups to a group, before another field of it or to its end. A subfield of a calculated field moves with its parent field. Available from Archicad 30.

projectInfoFields.description: The fields of the Project Info groups to move, in the order the moves are made. A subfield of a calculated field cannot be moved on its own, it moves with its parent field.

projectInfoGroupId.description: The group to move the field to. To reorder a field within its group, give its current group.

beforeProjectInfoFieldId.description: The field of the target group to move the field before. When omitted, the field is moved to the end of the group.

example.description: Creates a custom Project Info field, moves it to the top of the first group with MoveProjectInfoFields, then deletes it. Requires Archicad 30 or later.
example.code:
"""Creates a custom Project Info field, moves it to the top of the first group with MoveProjectInfoFields, then deletes it.

Requires Archicad 30 or later.
"""
import aclib

firstGroup = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectInfoGroups')['projectInfoGroups'][0]

created = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateProjectInfoFields', {
    'projectInfoFields': [{'projectInfoName': 'Tapir Example Field', 'projectInfoGroupId': firstGroup['projectInfoGroupId']}]
})['fields'][0]
if 'projectInfoFieldId' not in created:
    raise SystemExit ('The field could not be created.')
fieldId = created['projectInfoFieldId']

move = {'projectInfoFieldId': fieldId, 'projectInfoGroupId': firstGroup['projectInfoGroupId']}
if firstGroup['fields']:
    move['beforeProjectInfoFieldId'] = firstGroup['fields'][0]['projectInfoFieldId']
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('MoveProjectInfoFields', {'projectInfoFields': [move]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectInfoGroups')

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteProjectInfoFields', {'projectInfoFieldIds': [{'projectInfoFieldId': fieldId}]})

commands.name: GetProjectInfoGroups
commands.description: Retrieves the Project Info groups in their order, each with its fields: id, name, value and, when exactly one project info autotext has the name of the field, the autotext key that SetProjectInfoField takes. Available from Archicad 30.

example.description: Prints the Project Info groups in their order, each with its fields, with GetProjectInfoGroups. Requires Archicad 30 or later.

Requires Archicad 30 or later.
"""

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectInfoGroups'))

commands.name: CreateProjectInfoGroups
commands.description: Creates Project Info groups with the given names, at the end of the group list. Available from Archicad 30.

projectInfoGroups.description: The Project Info groups to create, in order. Each is added to the end of the group list.

name.description: The name of the new group. It must not be used by another group.

example.description: Creates a Project Info group at the end of the group list with CreateProjectInfoGroups, then deletes it. Requires Archicad 30 or later.
example.code:
"""Creates a Project Info group at the end of the group list with CreateProjectInfoGroups, then deletes it.

Requires Archicad 30 or later.
"""
import aclib

created = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateProjectInfoGroups', {
    'projectInfoGroups': [{'name': 'Tapir Example Group'}]
})['projectInfoGroupIdsOrErrors'][0]
aclib.PrintJson (created)
if 'error' in created:
    raise SystemExit ('The group could not be created.')

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectInfoGroups')

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteProjectInfoGroups', {'projectInfoGroups': [{'projectInfoGroupId': created['projectInfoGroupId']}]})

commands.name: RenameProjectInfoGroups
commands.description: Renames Project Info groups. Available from Archicad 30.

projectInfoGroups.description: The Project Info groups to rename, each with its new name.

example.description: Creates a Project Info group, renames it with RenameProjectInfoGroups, then deletes it. Requires Archicad 30 or later.

commands.name: DeleteProjectInfoGroups
commands.description: Deletes Project Info groups. A group that contains fixed (built-in) fields cannot be deleted. Available from Archicad 30.

projectInfoGroups.description: The Project Info groups to delete. A group that contains fixed (built-in) fields cannot be deleted.

example.description: Creates a Project Info group and deletes it with DeleteProjectInfoGroups. A group that holds built-in fields cannot be deleted. Requires Archicad 30 or later.

commands.name: MoveProjectInfoGroups
commands.description: Moves Project Info groups before another group, or to the end of the group list when no other group is given. Available from Archicad 30.

projectInfoGroups.description: The Project Info groups to move, in the order the moves are made.

example.description: Creates a Project Info group, moves it before the first group with MoveProjectInfoGroups, then deletes it. Without beforeProjectInfoGroupId a group moves to the end of the list. Requires Archicad 30 or later.

commands.name: GetStories
commands.description: Retrieves information about the story structure of the currently loaded project: index, floor id, name, level, height and, from Archicad 28, the IFC GlobalId of each story.

skipNullFloor.description: Floor indices above ground-floor level may start with 1 instead of 0.

example.description: Prints the stories of the project (index, name, level, height) with GetStories.
example.code:
"""Prints the stories of the project (index, name, level, height) with GetStories."""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetStories'))

commands.name: SetStories
commands.description: Sets the story structure of the currently loaded project to the given list of stories. Existing stories outside the list are deleted, and Archicad deletes every element whose home story they are with them; dryRun lists those stories with the number of elements on each, without changing anything. To add, change or delete a single story, use InsertStory or DeleteStory instead.

dryRun.description: If true, nothing is changed in the project and no undo step is created: the list is checked as in a real run, and the response lists the existing stories a real run would delete (with the number of elements Archicad would delete with each) and the number of stories it would insert. Default is false.

success.description: Whether the story structure was set, or on a dry run, whether the list passed the checks a real run makes first.

wouldDeleteStories.description: Only on a successful dry run: the existing stories a real run would delete, from the bottom up. Empty when it would delete none.

name.description: The name of the story.

elementCount.description: The number of elements whose home story is the story (in the floor plan database): Archicad deletes them together with it.

wouldInsertStoryCount.description: Only on a successful dry run: the number of new stories a real run would add below and above the existing ones until they reach the requested indices. When the requested indices leave a gap above or below the existing stories, this includes the stories in the gap, which the real run deletes again.

example.description: Renames the top story with SetStories, reads the stories back, then restores the original names. SetStories takes the whole story structure: stories left out are deleted, new ones are created. A dry run first shows what leaving out the top story would delete (the story and the number of elements on it) without changing anything.
example.code:
"""Renames the top story with SetStories, reads the stories back, then restores the original names.

SetStories takes the whole story structure: stories left out are deleted, new ones are created.
A dry run first shows what leaving out the top story would delete (the story and the number
of elements on it) without changing anything.
"""
import aclib

stories = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetStories')['stories']
original = [
    {'index': s['index'], 'dispOnSections': s['dispOnSections'], 'level': s['level'], 'name': s['name']}
    for s in stories
]

if len (original) > 1:
    aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetStories', {'stories': original[:-1], 'dryRun': True}))

changed = [dict (s) for s in original]
changed[-1]['name'] = 'Tapir Top Story'
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetStories', {'stories': changed}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetStories')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetStories', {'stories': original}))

commands.name: InsertStory
commands.description: Inserts one new story directly above or below an existing story, with its name, height and level line display, and returns the new story as GetStories reports it. Other stories are never deleted; their indices and levels can change with the insertion as in Archicad's Story Settings dialog, so read them again with GetStories.

storyIndex.description: The index of an existing story (see GetStories) next to which the new story is inserted.

position.description: Whether the new story is inserted directly above or directly below the story of storyIndex.

name.description: The name of the new story. Default is an empty name.

height.description: The height of the new story, greater than zero. Default is the height of the story of storyIndex.

dispOnSections.description: Whether the level line of the new story appears on sections and elevations. Default is what Archicad gives a new story.

story.description: The new story, as GetStories reports it after the insertion.

example.description: Inserts a new story above the top story with InsertStory, prints it, then deletes it again with DeleteStory. Unlike SetStories, InsertStory only adds a story; no other story is deleted.
example.code:
"""Inserts a new story above the top story with InsertStory, prints it, then deletes it again with DeleteStory.

Unlike SetStories, InsertStory only adds a story; no other story is deleted.
"""
import aclib

aclib.raiseOnError = True

stories = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetStories')
newStory = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('InsertStory', {
    'storyIndex': stories['lastStory'],
    'position': 'Above',
    'name': 'Tapir Roof Terrace',
    'height': 3.0,
    'dispOnSections': True
})['story']
aclib.PrintJson (newStory)

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteStory', {'storyIndex': newStory['index']}))

commands.name: DeleteStory
commands.description: Deletes one story. Archicad deletes every element whose home story it is together with it, so a story that is the home story of any element is only deleted with deleteElements: true; otherwise it fails and gives the number of those elements. dryRun reports, without changing anything, whether the story would be deleted and how many elements with it.

storyIndex.description: The index of the story to delete (see GetStories).

deleteElements.description: Archicad deletes every element whose home story is the deleted story. Without true here, a story that is the home story of any element is not deleted, and the response says how many elements it has. Default is false.

success.description: Whether the story was deleted, or on a dry run, whether a real run would delete it.

wouldDelete.description: Present, and true, on a dry run that a real run would delete the story.

elementCount.description: The number of elements whose home story is the story (in the floor plan database): the elements deleted with it, or that kept it from being deleted. Absent when the story was not found.

example.description: Inserts a story, places a wall on it, and deletes the story with DeleteStory. A story that is the home story of elements is only deleted with deleteElements: true, because Archicad deletes those elements with it. A dry run first tells how many elements that would be.
example.code:
"""Inserts a story, places a wall on it, and deletes the story with DeleteStory.

A story that is the home story of elements is only deleted with deleteElements: true, because Archicad
deletes those elements with it. A dry run first tells how many elements that would be.
"""
import aclib

aclib.raiseOnError = True

stories = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetStories')
story = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('InsertStory', {
    'storyIndex': stories['lastStory'],
    'position': 'Above',
    'name': 'Tapir Story To Delete',
    'height': 3.0
})['story']

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWalls', {'wallsData': [{
    'begCoordinate': {'x': 700.0, 'y': 700.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 705.0, 'y': 700.0},
    'floorIndex': story['index'], 'zCoordinate': 0.0, 'height': 2.5, 'thickness': 0.2
}]})

# Refused without deleteElements: the response gives the number of elements on the story.
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteStory', {'storyIndex': story['index']}, raiseOnError = False))

# What a real run would do, without changing anything.
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteStory', {'storyIndex': story['index'], 'deleteElements': True, 'dryRun': True}))

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteStory', {'storyIndex': story['index'], 'deleteElements': True}))

commands.name: ModifyStory
commands.description: Changes the name, level, height or level line display of one story, and returns the story as GetStories reports it. It never adds or deletes a story. level moves only this story; height moves every story above with the top of this one, as in Archicad's Story Settings dialog. The elements of a moved story move with it.

storyIndex.description: The index of the story to modify (see GetStories).

name.description: The new name of the story.

level.description: The new level of the story. Only this story moves: the story below gets taller or shorter, and the stories above stay where they are unless height is given too. It must stay above the level of the story below, and, without height, below the level of the story above. On the top story without height its top stays where it is: moving it up makes it shorter by as much, and moving it down taller.

height.description: The new height of the story, greater than zero. As in Archicad's Story Settings dialog, every story above moves up or down with the top of this story and keeps its height.

dispOnSections.description: Whether the level line of the story appears on sections and elevations.

story.description: The modified story, as GetStories reports it after the change.

example.description: Inserts a story above the top story, renames it, changes its height and level with ModifyStory, then deletes it again. Unlike SetStories, ModifyStory changes one story and never adds or deletes one. A new height moves the stories above with the top of the story; a new level moves only the story itself.
example.code:
"""Inserts a story above the top story, renames it, changes its height and level with ModifyStory, then deletes it again.

Unlike SetStories, ModifyStory changes one story and never adds or deletes one. A new height moves the
stories above with the top of the story; a new level moves only the story itself.
"""
import aclib

aclib.raiseOnError = True

stories = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetStories')
story = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('InsertStory', {
    'storyIndex': stories['lastStory'],
    'position': 'Above',
    'name': 'Tapir Story To Modify',
    'height': 3.0
})['story']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyStory', {
    'storyIndex': story['index'],
    'name': 'Tapir Modified Story',
    'height': 3.5,
    'dispOnSections': False
}))

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyStory', {
    'storyIndex': story['index'],
    'level': story['level'] + 0.5
}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteStory', {'storyIndex': story['index']})

commands.name: GetAutoTextKeys
commands.description: Retrieves the available autotext keys (name and embeddable key): the Project Info, layout, drawing, date and other autotexts Archicad lists, and the property based ones, optionally for a specific element. Embed a key in a Text or Label content by surrounding it with '<' and '>'.

elementId.description: Optional. The element to retrieve context dependent autotext keys for (its own properties, plus the ones common to all element types, e.g. 'Element ID', 'Area'). When omitted, only the property based autotext keys common to all element types are returned. The other autotexts (Project Info, layout, drawing, date, ...) are returned either way.

name.description: The autotext's name, as shown in the Insert Autotext dialog of Archicad.

key.description: The autotext's key. To embed it in the content of a Text or Label element, surround it with '<' and '>', e.g. '<PROJECTNAME>' or '<PROPERTY-69A58F6F-DD3B-478D-B5EF-09A16BD0C548>'.

example.description: Prints the autotext keys (name and key) that a Text or Label can embed as <KEY>, with GetAutoTextKeys. Pass an elementId to get the keys of that element's type as well.
example.code:
"""Prints the autotext keys (name and key) that a Text or Label can embed as <KEY>, with GetAutoTextKeys.

Pass an elementId to get the keys of that element's type as well.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAutoTextKeys', {}))

commands.name: GetAutoTextName
commands.description: Retrieves the display names of one or more autotext keys (as returned inside a '<...>' embedded key), with a direct guid lookup for property-based keys instead of enumerating every property definition.

keys.description: Autotext keys as returned by GetAutoTextKeys or GetProjectInfoFields (without the surrounding '<' and '>'), e.g. 'PROPERTY-69A58F6F-DD3B-478D-B5EF-09A16BD0C548' or 'PROJECTNAME'.

example.description: Prints the display names of two autotext keys with GetAutoTextName.
example.code:
"""Prints the display names of two autotext keys with GetAutoTextName."""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAutoTextName', {'keys': ['PROJECTNAME', 'PROJECTNUMBER']}))

commands.name: GetAllAutoTextKeys
commands.description: Retrieves every autotext key Archicad knows (not only the property-based ones returned by GetAutoTextKeys) with its current value, resolved without an element context.

key.description: The autotext's key. To embed it in the content of a Text or Label element, surround it with '<' and '>'.

value.description: The autotext's current value, as Archicad resolves it without an element context.

example.description: Prints the first autotext keys Archicad knows, each with its current value, with GetAllAutoTextKeys. The values are resolved without an element context; the keys and values depend on the project, the Archicad version and the UI language.
example.code:
"""Prints the first autotext keys Archicad knows, each with its current value, with GetAllAutoTextKeys.

The values are resolved without an element context; the keys and values depend on the project,
the Archicad version and the UI language.
"""
import aclib

autoTexts = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAllAutoTextKeys', {})['autoTexts']
print (f'{len (autoTexts)} autotext keys, the first ones:')
aclib.PrintJson (autoTexts[:10])

commands.name: InterpretAutoTexts
commands.description: Resolves one or more autotexts (e.g. '<LAYOUTID>') to their values, optionally in the context of an element, so a key can be tested before it is written into a Text or Label.

autoTexts.description: The autotexts to resolve, either as they are written in the content of a Text or Label element, e.g. '<LAYOUTID>' or '<PROPERTY-69A58F6F-DD3B-478D-B5EF-09A16BD0C548>', or as bare keys without the surrounding '<' and '>', e.g. 'LAYOUTID'.

elementId.description: Optional. The element in whose context the autotexts are resolved, e.g. a Text on a layout for layout autotexts. When omitted, they are resolved without an element context.

values.description: One result per input autotext, in the same order.

value.description: The resolved value of the autotext.

example.description: Resolves the project name autotext to its value with InterpretAutoTexts. An autotext can be given as written in a Text ('<PROJECTNAME>') or as a bare key ('PROJECTNAME'). Pass an elementId (e.g. of a Text on a layout) to resolve them in that element's context.
example.code:
"""Resolves the project name autotext to its value with InterpretAutoTexts.

An autotext can be given as written in a Text ('<PROJECTNAME>') or as a bare key ('PROJECTNAME').
Pass an elementId (e.g. of a Text on a layout) to resolve them in that element's context.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('InterpretAutoTexts', {
    'autoTexts': ['<PROJECTNAME>', 'PROJECTNAME']
}))

commands.name: GetNoteAutotexts
commands.description: Retrieves the autotexts available in the notes of an element type (e.g. a Dimension), each with the element types it is available for. The autotexts are identified by the numeric value of their API_NoteAutotextID. For a Dimension, the optional dimensionAppearance (Linear by default) chooses the dimension type. Needs Archicad 26 or later.

noteOwnerType.description: The type of the element that owns the note, e.g. 'Dimension', 'RadialDimension', 'LevelDimension' or 'AngleDimension'.

dimensionAppearance.description: Optional dimension type, as in the Dimension Settings, whose note autotexts are listed when noteOwnerType is 'Dimension'. Defaults to Linear. Not allowed with other owner types.

noteAutotexts.description: The autotexts available in the notes of the given owner type, in ascending order of autotextId.

example.description: Prints the autotexts available in the notes of linear and of elevation dimensions, with GetNoteAutotexts. For noteOwnerType 'Dimension' the optional dimensionAppearance (Linear, Cumulative, Baseline or Elevation) chooses the dimension type; it defaults to Linear. Requires Archicad 26 or later.
example.code:
"""Prints the autotexts available in the notes of linear and of elevation dimensions, with GetNoteAutotexts.

For noteOwnerType 'Dimension' the optional dimensionAppearance (Linear, Cumulative, Baseline or
Elevation) chooses the dimension type; it defaults to Linear.

Requires Archicad 26 or later.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetNoteAutotexts', {'noteOwnerType': 'Dimension'}))
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetNoteAutotexts', {'noteOwnerType': 'Dimension', 'dimensionAppearance': 'Elevation'}))

commands.name: GetNoteAutoTextKeywords
commands.description: Retrieves the keywords of note autotexts (the autotexts of dimension, label and other element notes) by their numeric API_NoteAutotextID values. Available from Archicad 26.

autoTextIds.description: Numeric values of the API_NoteAutotextID enumeration of the Archicad API (the autotexts of dimension, label and other element notes).

keywords.description: One result per input id, in the same order.

example.description: Prints the keywords of the autotexts available in dimension notes with GetNoteAutoTextKeywords. Requires Archicad 26 or later.

commands.name: GetHotlinks
commands.description: Gets the file system locations (path) of the hotlink modules and the instance elements placed from each node. The hotlinks can have tree hierarchy in the project.

example.description: Prints the hotlink nodes of the project (source file, name, type, placed instances and children) with GetHotlinks.
example.code:
"""Prints the hotlink nodes of the project (source file, name, type, placed instances and children) with GetHotlinks."""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetHotlinks'))

commands.name: CreateHotlinkNodes
commands.description: Creates hotlink module nodes from source files. A node that already points at the same file is returned instead of duplicated (Archicad 26 and later; 25 cannot see an unplaced node).

hotlinkNodes.description: The hotlink module nodes to create. A node that already points at the same source file (compared case-insensitively) is returned as it is, with existing: true, and the name and story settings asked for are ignored. On Archicad 25 a node that has not been placed yet cannot be found, so a repeated request there creates a second node.

sourceLocation.description: Absolute path of the module source file (.mod or .pln).

name.description: Optional display name of the node. Defaults to the file name. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.

storyRangeType.description: Optional. Which stories of the source are placed: all of them, or the single reference story. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.

refFloorIndex.description: Optional index of the reference story in the source file. Defaults to 0. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.

hotlinkNodes.description: One item per requested node, in order: the node guid with its existing flag, or an error.

example.description: Saves the first wall as a module in the temp folder, creates a hotlink node from it with CreateHotlinkNodes, then deletes the node. Needs at least one Wall.

commands.name: CreateHotlinkInstances
commands.description: Places instances of hotlink module nodes at an origin, rotation and mirroring.

example.description: Places an instance of a hotlink node at (50, 0), rotated by 30 degrees, with CreateHotlinkInstances. The node is made from the first wall, saved as a module in the temp folder; at the end the node is deleted with its instance. Needs at least one Wall.
example.code:
"""Places an instance of a hotlink node at (50, 0), rotated by 30 degrees, with CreateHotlinkInstances.

The node is made from the first wall, saved as a module in the temp folder; at the end the node is
deleted with its instance. Needs at least one Wall.
"""
import math
import os
import tempfile
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunCommand ('API.GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')
modulePath = os.path.join (tempfile.mkdtemp (), 'TapirExample.mod')
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SaveAsModuleFile', {'moduleFilePath': modulePath, 'elements': walls})
nodeId = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateHotlinkNodes', {'hotlinkNodes': [{'sourceLocation': modulePath}]})['hotlinkNodes'][0]['hotlinkNodeId']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateHotlinkInstances', {
    'hotlinkInstances': [{
        'hotlinkNodeId': nodeId,
        'origin': {'x': 50.0, 'y': 0.0},
        'rotationAngle': math.radians (30),
        'mirrored': False
    }]
}))

commands.name: MergeFile
commands.description: Merges an Archicad project or module file into the model, as File > Interoperability > Merge does, at an origin, rotation and mirroring, each story of the file on the story with the same index (or from floorIndex on). The Archicad API has no merge, so the file is placed as a hotlink and the hotlink is broken, in one undo step, and the elements that are new afterwards are returned; Archicad leaves them grouped together. A file the project already hotlinks is refused, because breaking would break that hotlink too.

sourceLocation.description: Absolute path of the file to merge: an Archicad project (.pln, .pla) or module (.mod). It cannot be a file the project already hotlinks: breaking that hotlink would turn its placed instances into ordinary elements too.

origin.description: Optional. Where the origin of the file lands in the project. Defaults to the project origin; if z is omitted, it is 0.

rotationAngle.description: Optional rotation about the origin, counter-clockwise, in radians. Defaults to 0.

mirrored.description: Optional. Reflects the file's local X axis before the rotation. Defaults to false.

floorIndex.description: Optional story of the project that the story with index 0 of the file goes to; the other stories of the file follow it. Defaults to 0, so each story of the file goes to the story with the same index.

elements.description: The elements the merge added to the model, every element of the file's model. Archicad leaves them grouped together, as it leaves the elements of a broken hotlink; UngroupElements dissolves the group.

example.description: Merges a module file into the project with MergeFile, 10 m north of where it was saved. The script saves a wall it creates as a module in a temporary folder first; the wall and the merged elements are deleted at the end. Requires Archicad 27 or later (SaveAsModuleFile with an element list).
example.code:
"""Merges a module file into the project with MergeFile, 10 m north of where it was saved.

The script saves a wall it creates as a module in a temporary folder first; the wall and the merged
elements are deleted at the end. Requires Archicad 27 or later (SaveAsModuleFile with an element list).
"""
import os
import tempfile

import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWalls', {'wallsData': [
    {'begCoordinate': {'x': 100.0, 'y': 100.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 104.0, 'y': 100.0}, 'height': 3.0, 'floorIndex': 0}
]})['elements']
modulePath = os.path.join (tempfile.mkdtemp (), 'TapirMergeFileExample.mod')
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SaveAsModuleFile', {'moduleFilePath': modulePath, 'elements': walls})

# The file's origin lands at (0, 10): the merged wall runs from (100, 110) to (104, 110).
merged = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('MergeFile', {'sourceLocation': modulePath, 'origin': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 10.0}})
aclib.PrintJson (merged)

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': walls + merged['elements']})
os.remove (modulePath)

example.description: Turns Auto-Intersection off with SetAutoIntersect, reads it back, then restores the previous state. It is a setting of the running Archicad, not of the project.
example.code:
"""Turns Auto-Intersection off with SetAutoIntersect, reads it back, then restores the previous state.

It is a setting of the running Archicad, not of the project.
"""
import aclib

originalIsOn = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAutoIntersect')['isOn']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetAutoIntersect', {'isOn': False}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAutoIntersect')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetAutoIntersect', {'isOn': originalIsOn}))

commands.name: ResolveNames
commands.description: Looks up words or phrases (for example from a user's question) among the names of the open project before they are passed to other commands: stories, layers, layer combinations, building materials, composites, profiles, surfaces, fills, lines, zone categories, element types (by API name and, from Archicad 27, by the name the Archicad interface shows), properties (by name, and by group and name together) and classifications (systems by name and version, items of every system by name and ID). For each name it returns 'found' with the items named exactly so, 'closeMatches' with the nearest names, best first (ranked by differences in case, accents, spacing and separators, shared words, one name containing the other and a few differing characters), or 'notFound' when nothing in the project is close, meaning the project has no such item and it must not be guessed. Each match carries what the other commands take: the story index, the attribute id and index, the elementType, the propertyId (with the property's group, value type and the classification items a custom property is available for), or the classificationSystemId and classificationItemId. Matching is lexical and deterministic. Read only.

names.description: The words or phrases to look up in the open project, for example taken from a user's question.

name.description: The word or phrase.

kind.description: The kind of item the word names. When it is left out, every kind is searched.

maxCloseMatches.description: The most close matches returned for one word, best first. The default is 5.

results.description: One result for each of the given names, in the same order.

name.description: The given word or phrase.

status.description: found: an item of the project has exactly this name (see found). closeMatches: no item has exactly this name, but some are close (see closeMatches). notFound: nothing in the project is close to it; the project has no such item, so it must not be guessed.

found.description: The items named exactly so (the same characters), with match 'exact'. More than one when items of different kinds, or several stories, have the name.

closeMatches.description: When nothing is named exactly so: the nearest items, best first. Empty when the status is found or notFound.

example.description: Checks words from a user's question against the open project with ResolveNames before using them: a story, a building material, an element type, a property, a classification and a word looked up among every kind of name. Each result says whether the project has an item named exactly so (found), only similar names (closeMatches, best first) or nothing close (notFound). A matched property carries the propertyId that GetPropertyValuesOfElements takes, a matched classification item its classificationSystemId and classificationItemId.
example.code:
"""Checks words from a user's question against the open project with ResolveNames before using them:
a story, a building material, an element type, a property, a classification and a word looked up
among every kind of name. Each result says whether the project has an item named exactly so (found),
only similar names (closeMatches, best first) or nothing close (notFound). A matched property carries
the propertyId that GetPropertyValuesOfElements takes, a matched classification item its
classificationSystemId and classificationItemId."""
import aclib

response = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ResolveNames', {
    'names': [
        {'name': 'ground floor', 'kind': 'Story'},
        {'name': 'concrete', 'kind': 'BuildingMaterial'},
        {'name': 'door', 'kind': 'ElementType'},
        {'name': 'fire rating', 'kind': 'Property'},
        {'name': 'wall', 'kind': 'Classification'},
        {'name': 'Fire Rating'}
    ],
    'maxCloseMatches': 3
})
aclib.PrintJson (response)

for result in response['results']:
    matches = result['found'] or result['closeMatches']
    print (result['name'], '->', result['status'], [(match['kind'], match['name']) for match in matches])
